clue.text: Error by team in a flying manoeuvre

blocks.note: a side is a team in sport
a slip is a small mistake

explanation.surface: A display team botches a stunt at an air show.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the reverse order of the clue: 'Error by team' puts the error after the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideslip is an aircraft moving sideways and downward, a deliberate pilot technique for losing height.

clue.text: Unusual way over the mountains

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means sitting above, so the first piece is written on top

blocks.note: St is short for street, a way
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: An odd route that takes travellers over the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unusual both describe something out of the ordinary or hard to explain.

clue.text: Study contains Bible version left in a desk

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a den is a private study
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A study has a Bible tucked away in a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the Authorized Version, is the King James Bible of 1611.
explanation.definitionFit: A davenport is a small writing desk with a sloping top and drawers at the side.

clue.text: Wise guy, the song-writer

blocks.note: first meaning: the Israelite king famed for wisdom
second meaning: the traditional author of the Song of Songs in the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise guy' sounds like a smart alec, but it means a man of great wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon is proverbially wise, and the biblical Song of Songs bears his name as its author.

clue.text: Concentrated in verbal form

blocks.note: taken as written
a tense is a form of a verb showing time

explanation.surface: Something expressed in a strong, concentrated form of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong and focused, like a concentrated flavour or a concentrated effort.

clue.text: Influenza took a firm hold but finally died away

indicators.note: something that has finally died away is gone at the end, so a closing letter d is removed

blocks.note: to grip something is to hold it firmly

explanation.surface: A bout of flu takes hold of someone, then fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the abbreviation for died, and here it is the last letter of GRIPPED that dies away, leaving GRIPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grippe is an old word, borrowed from French, for flu, the viral illness with fever and aches.

clue.text: Explosive — counting to drop one, possibly?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter leaves the phrase
possibly hints at one of several arrangements the letters could take

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A countdown to an explosion, where you stop just before reaching one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gun-cotton is nitrocellulose, cotton treated with nitric acid to make a powerful explosive.

clue.text: Society leader sadly ruined without being covered

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are knocked out of order
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round another

blocks.note: the opening letter of Society
taken as written

explanation.surface: A society figure's ruin is made worse by having no insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' is both the anagram fodder and a word that sounds like an anagram signal; 'sadly' is the true one.
explanation.definitionFit: To be insured is to have a policy protecting against loss, so being covered by insurance.

clue.text: Standard note about a put-up job in summer-time

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
taken as written
sol, or soh, is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A routine note about a rigged scheme carried out in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: A put-up job is a fraud, but here it is literal: something put up, as a sunshade is in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella opened to give shade from the sun in hot weather.

clue.text: Civil upheaval which the world experiences every day

definitions.text: which the world experiences every day

blocks.note: first meaning: the overthrow of a government by its people

blocks.clueFragment: which the world experiences every day
blocks.note: second meaning: one full turn of a body on its axis

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like a gloomy comment on politics, but it is astronomy: the Earth spins once a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a political uprising and a single complete rotation, such as Earth makes daily.

clue.text: Active as a party, getting rid of odd members

indicators.note: the members are the letters, and getting rid of the odd-numbered ones keeps only the even ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: A political party sheds its awkward members to become more lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd members' sounds like eccentric party members being expelled, but it means letters one, three, five and seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially an older person still moving briskly.

clue.text: Game suggesting people's appearance in the square dance

definitions.text: Game suggesting people's appearance in the square dance

blocks.clueFragment: Game suggesting people's appearance in the square dance
blocks.note: surface reading: a game that looks like a group of dancers lined up in a square

blocks.clueFragment: people's appearance in the square dance
blocks.note: setter's reading: a square number of men, three times three, doing a traditional English folk dance

explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance done by groups of men with bells and sticks; nine is the square of three.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old board game where each player has nine pieces, played on a grid of nested squares.

clue.text: Wait, say, to follow directions and proclaim the answer

indicators.note: say asks us to take the word wait as it is spoken, which is also how a measure of heaviness is spoken
to follow tells us the first piece comes after the next one in the finished word

blocks.note: E and N are east and north, two compass directions
wait spoken aloud is weight, and an ounce is a weight

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pause, head off in a given direction and announce the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks both the sound of wait and an example: weight, say an ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is a formal verb meaning to state or declare something clearly, close to announce.

clue.text: This way to the cabin, chum

blocks.note: first meaning: on a ship, the hatch and stairway leading down to the cabins
second meaning: a friend or mate

explanation.walkthrough: On a ship the companion, or companionway, is the staircase or hatch giving access below deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a friend and the nautical hatchway or staircase down to a ship's cabins.

clue.text: Rick's supporter takes burden round the end of it

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
to go round something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to saddle someone is to burden them
the closing letter of this short word

explanation.surface: Someone named Rick has a loyal backer who shoulders the burden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick looks like a man's name, but a rick is a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: A staddle is a raised stone or timber base on which a haystack is built to keep it dry.

clue.text: All work and no play makes one a failure as this

definitions.text: All work and no play makes one a failure as this

blocks.note: surface reading: the proverb about Jack becoming dull from too much toil

blocks.clueFragment: makes one a failure as this
blocks.note: setter's reading: a writer of stage works who never produces a play has failed in that job

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'all work and no play makes Jack a dull boy' is turned: play here means a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is someone who writes plays, so one with no plays would be no success.

clue.text: Japanese pottery with a new wine as returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
must is grape juice that has not yet fermented into wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Japanese ceramics come back with a bottle of young wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satsuma' looks like it should be the orange, but here it is the ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma is a cream-coloured, crackle-glazed earthenware named after a former province in southern Japan.

clue.text: Egghead, for example, produces a set of records in French

blocks.note: an album is a set of records issued together
en is French for in

explanation.surface: An intellectual releases an album of French songs.
explanation.walkthrough: An egghead is an intellectual, but here 'egghead' is read as the top of an egg: the white sits around and above the yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is egg white, the clear protein-rich part surrounding the yolk inside the shell.

clue.text: Sink ship that's a coal container

blocks.note: first meaning: to sink a vessel deliberately by holing it
second meaning: a metal bucket for carrying coal to a fire

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship carrying coal; the clue really holds two unrelated meanings joined by 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deliberately sinking one's own vessel and a lidded bucket kept beside a fireplace.

clue.text: Entering in ship, Peter joins in team

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one name is placed within another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
SS is short for steamship
Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up

explanation.surface: A man called Peter boards a ship and joins the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: To inspan is a South African word for harnessing oxen or horses to a wagon, so the team is a team of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspans means yokes animals together into a team for pulling, the reverse of outspans.

clue.text: Bill is ready to sing

blocks.note: first meaning: a document asking for payment
second meaning, read as two words: in good singing form

explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name about to sing; split the answer as 'in voice' for the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill for goods or services, and a singer in voice is ready to perform.

clue.text: Hamlet's rest — resembling Palgrave's Treasury?

blocks.note: first meaning: Hamlet's dying words are 'the rest is' this
second meaning: Palgrave compiled 'The Golden Treasury', and the proverb says this is golden

explanation.walkthrough: Francis Palgrave's anthology is 'The Golden Treasury' of English verse, and the proverb runs 'speech is silver, but this is golden'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet ends with 'The rest is silence', and the proverb calls the same quiet golden, like Palgrave's Treasury.

clue.text: Send a small replacement for normal starter to solve this tangle

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
a replacement for something takes its place, so one letter is swapped out for new ones

blocks.note: taken as written
wee is Scottish for small
the starting letter of normal

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch a small spare part to sort out a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangle is a large brown kelp, so 'this tangle' is one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for oarweed or kelp, the large brown seaweeds of the lower shore.

clue.text: In I go with a valuable form of garden embellishment

indicators.note: a new form of something is the same material shaped differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strolls into a garden carrying something precious that adorns it.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling with -LLAEA is the older one; today it is usually written bougainvillea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bougainvillaea is a climbing shrub with vivid papery bracts, grown to decorate walls and gardens.

clue.text: Issue shows the fourth dimension in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: physics treats time as the fourth dimension after the three of space

explanation.surface: A science magazine issue features time travel and hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, as a chimney issues smoke.

clue.text: Wherein advance is made on the narrowest front - record held by Clive?

definitions.text: Wherein advance is made on the narrowest front

blocks.clueFragment: Wherein advance is made on the narrowest front
blocks.note: first meaning: a line of people walking one behind another
second meaning: a file kept in the subcontinent by its famous British governor

explanation.walkthrough: Clive of India was the 18th-century soldier who secured British rule in Bengal, so a record of his would be an Indian file.
explanation.definitionFit: Single file, one person directly behind another, presents the smallest possible width to anyone ahead.

clue.text: Translation exercise, such as Gray's blushing flower?

blocks.note: first meaning: a passage set for translation without preparation
second meaning: Gray's Elegy says many a flower is born to blush without being seen

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' has the line 'Full many a flower is born to blush unseen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a school translation passage not seen beforehand and an adjective for something nobody observes.

clue.text: Vanquished by some exploit indeed

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here read off the front of indeed

blocks.note: read as two words, in deed: the second word is the outer piece
a feat is a notable exploit

explanation.surface: Someone was beaten by a truly remarkable achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' must be split into 'in deed': one word becomes the indicator and the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanquished and the answer both describe an opponent beaten or overcome in a contest.
